title: Pool Ops Sidecar: Health Timeline + Adaptive Burst Controls
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, horizontally scannable 'sidecar' panel for the Redwood Console that surfaces GPU pool health over time and exposes adaptive burst controls for Dedicated capacity. This ticket covers the visual timeline, alert summarization, quick actions (drain/evacuate/scale), and an inline adaptive burst configuration UX that lets operators tune burst budgets and priority rules without leaving the pool view.

Goals:
- Provide a single glance timeline for pool-level health signals (utilization, queue latency, OOM events, kernel requeue rate).
- Allow operators to change burst policies (burst budget, cooldown, preemptible tiers) in-context with clear SLO-critical warnings.
- Surface root-cause hints and links to deeper diagnostics (traces, logs, recent deploys).
- Keep the sidecar compact for small screens while allowing expansion for advanced settings.

Scope (in this ticket):
- Low-fidelity and high-fidelity comps for collapsed and expanded states.
- Interaction states for alert hover, timeline scrubbing, and configuration save/rollback flows.
- Accessibility pass for color contrast and keyboard-first controls.
- Handoff spec for engineering with tokens for metrics, event names, and API payload examples (referenced in design_links).

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Backend rollout orchestration (handled in ENG-9422) and telemetry sampling changes (ENG-9578).
acceptance_criteria: Collapsed sidecar shows a 7-day sparkline for CPU/GPU utilization and a concise alert badge count.
Expanded timeline allows scrubbing to a specific hour and shows correlated events (deploys, autoscale actions, OOMs).
Adaptive burst form includes percent-based budget, cooldown in minutes, and a radio for preemptible vs reserved tiers with inline validation.
Saving burst settings triggers a non-blocking, dismissible toast with an undo option that reverts to previous values for 30s.
Design tokens and layout constraints provided in the handoff doc; Figma file contains component variants and responsive breakpoints.
Accessibility checks: all interactive elements reachable by keyboard, labels present for ARIA, and color contrast meets AA for text and icons.
notes: Decision: prefer a stacked mini-timeline (utilization, queue-latency, errors) allowing color-coded overlays rather than separate charts to preserve vertical space.
Trade-off: overlaying series reduces immediate clarity for new users but improves density for experienced operators. Include a legend toggle to declutter.
Performance: timeline should use vector previews for quick render; full interactive timeline will fetch 1h resolution by default and lazy-load fine-grain samples on scrub.
Implementation hint: autoscale actions should be gated behind 'Confirm' when changing burst budget >50% to avoid accidental cost spikes.
Localization: labels and tooltips will need expansion for i18n; avoid hard-coded time units in images.
